name: Lemuel
overview: Lemuel is a male figure identified as a king who is quoted in Proverbs 31. Beyond his role as a king, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His mention is unique and specific to the wisdom literature of the Bible.
namesAndTitles: The name Lemuel means '[belonging] to G-d [El],' reflecting a theistic connection in its Hebrew origin. He is also referred to by the title 'King Lemuel,' which emphasizes his royal status as recorded in Proverbs 31:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Lemuel beyond his designation as a king in Proverbs 31. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Lemuel's significance lies in his role as the recipient of wisdom teachings in Proverbs 31, where he is instructed on righteous leadership and moral conduct. His inclusion in this passage highlights the biblical emphasis on godly guidance for rulers. Though little else is known about him, his mention serves to frame the wisdom imparted to kings as divinely inspired and authoritative.
